posts.author: OmaruS
posts.body: If you have it on Steam, you can probably just open it directly since it has a "SteamOS" icon on the shop. If that doesnt work or you do not have it there, you can add the engine as a "non-steam game" and then use Proton to run it. I do it with RPG Maker XP and it runs fine, so I think it will work fine as well for MV. But, if your chromebook is not that powerful, it will run quite slow because of Steam and the "layer" of Proton running on the PC. So there's a chance that using Wine will be better then using steam with proton.

I used to have Ubuntu, and run MV through Steam. When I did, MV  worked fairly well except for a couple of things that weren't vital. The battle=testing for troops in the editor didn't work, if I recall. Also, and more importantly, the 'Help' didn't function properly. 90% of the time that wasn't an issue, but, for example,  if you needed to know how to make a plugin register a picture with MV so that when you deploy a game the deployed game included and loaded the picture, it could be a bit of a pain.
